data.narrative:
Horizon Quantum Computing, a public-stage quantum computing company founded by Joe Fitzsimons, has raised $131M+ including a $110M PIPE in December 2025. The valuation assessment is anchored to a peer universe of five same-sector, same-stage companies spanning the quantum computing market.

The peer-median method represents the sole triangulation approach applicable to this stage and sector. The comparable set—IonQ ($13.0B), D-Wave Quantum ($6.3B), Rigetti Computing ($4.5B), Infleqtion ($1.9B), and Archer Materials ($60M)—yields a median valuation of $4.5B. This cohort exhibits substantial dispersion, with valuations ranging from $60M to $13.0B, reflecting early-stage quantum technology heterogeneity and varied commercial maturity across the peer set.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $3.8B (low), $4.5B (median), to $5.2B (high). This single-method framework carries material uncertainty given limited applicability of alternative valuation methodologies to pre-revenue or early-revenue quantum computing platforms. The wide peer range ($60M to $13.0B) signals that comparable-company multiples alone provide directional guidance rather than precision. Key unknowns include Horizon's quantum volume, qubit roadmap, customer pipeline relative to peers, and capital efficiency in deployed PIPE proceeds. Additional diligence on near-term revenue visibility and technological differentiation versus IonQ and D-Wave would substantially narrow this range.
